speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to assess your newborn's respiratory distress, so please describe the onset and severity of their breathing difficulties, including any cyanosis or grunting. Did the distress start immediately at birth or develop later, and are there any known maternal infections or risk factors?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the prematurity and the 2-hour delay in onset, I suspect transient tachypnea of the newborn rather than immediate RDS. Let's check the chest X-ray to look for fluid in the fissures or perihilar streaking. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest Radiograph shows fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of grunting, retractions, and cyanosis in a 33-week preterm infant is highly characteristic of surfactant deficiency rather than TTN. DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
